metadata.scope: Two defects in the nightly regression detector, both proven live at bf6353703. (1) tools/nightly_classify.py:92-104 excludes a benchmark from filing only when its category set is ENTIRELY infra, so a partial serving outage that produces MIXED trial pairs (one api_error + one compile_error) files GitHub issues anyway - this is how #520-#523 were filed on 2026-07-29 during a total serving failure of opencode-qwen3-5-35b-a3b-mxfp8. Fix: a benchmark is infra-tainted if ANY trial hit an infra category. (2) No run-level validity gate exists at all: nothing inspects the run in aggregate, so an unmeasurable run is partially believed AND banked unflagged into ~/.ailang/state/nightly-eval-history.jsonl, corrupting the m-nightly-flake-guard trailing window for the next 5 nights. Fix: an infra-taint-fraction gate (>=0.30 => INVALID, file nothing, one --type note) plus the M-EVAL-MEASUREMENT-CONTRACT validity vocabulary (970d90e29) applied to the JSONL - validity field, absent-means-VALID, default-exclude at read time, one-shot --mark-invalid backfill for 2026-07-29.

premises_refuted: R-A (LOUD - DEFECT 3 IS FALSE): tools/test_nightly_classify.py DOES run in CI. The root Makefile has no python because it does `include make/test.mk` (line 73), and make/test.mk:19-20 defines `test-nightly-classifier: @python3 tools/test_nightly_classify.py -v`. ci.yml:133-136 runs that make target in the `test` job, and ci.yml:138-144 ALREADY has an anti-vacuity guard (`::error::` if fewer than 20 '--- PASS:' lines). It is also a dependency of `make ci` (make/ci.mk:11). Ran it: 40 tests, OK, 40 PASS lines. The controller's greps missed it on both sides (root Makefile only; and CI invokes the make target, not the patterns searched). A regression test added by this sprint WILL execute in CI. The planned 'make the tests reachable' milestone is DELETED. The sibling flake-guard sprint's R-D anticipated this exact trap and fixed it in M4.6 - defect 3 was a re-derivation of an already-solved problem.

R-B (unverified claim CONFIRMED and QUANTIFIED - larger than suspected): the polluted 2026-07-29 night corrupts the trailing window for exactly 5 nights (2026-07-30..2026-08-03; select_window takes the 5 most recent DISTINCT dates strictly before tonight). Measured by replaying a hypothetical 2026-07-30 all-fail for each bench with and without the 07-29 records: 12 of 42 benchmarks get a DIFFERENT verdict. 10 are FALSE NEGATIVES (9 REGRESSION->SUSPECTED-FLAKE, 1 REGRESSION->GAP) - a real regression would go unpaged, silently; 5 of those had a perfectly green 10/10 window dragged to 8-9/10, i.e. the exact solid->broken signal the detector exists to catch. 2 are FALSE POSITIVES (SUSPECTED-FLAKE->REGRESSION) via consecutive_failures, which is NOT windowed - it walks back until a night with passes!=0, so 07-29 inflates the escalation counter by +1 until the bench next passes.
R-C: '~0.5d' is wrong for the work as scoped. Bottom-up estimate is 9h. See estimate_delta_from_mission for the attribution and the cut line that does fit 0.5d.
additional_findings: F-1: the CI anti-skip floor is STALE and now weak - ci.yml:141 fails only below 20 PASS lines while the suite emits 40. F-2: the any-infra fix ALONE would have prevented all four false issues. Per-night suppression over the real corpus (filed-today -> suppressed): 07-24 6->1, 07-25 7->1, 07-26 4->0, 07-27 5->2, 07-28 8->0, 07-29 7->7. So on the incident night it suppresses 100% of filings. Fixing defect 1 alone leaves all 12 verdict flips intact.

metadata.decision_threshold: PREDICATE: infra_taint_fraction = |{bench : ANY trial's error_category in INFRA_CATEGORIES}| / |benches parsed|. INVALID iff benches_parsed == 0 (reason 'zero_files', existing vocabulary) OR infra_taint_fraction >= 0.30 (reason 'infra_outage', ONE new constant). Exposed as --invalid-infra-fraction (default 0.30). BEHAVIOUR ON ALL SIX MEASURED NIGHTS: 07-24 0.048 VALID, 07-25 0.024 VALID, 07-26 0.048 VALID, 07-27 0.048 VALID, 07-28 0.048 VALID, 07-29 1.000 INVALID. Zero false positives across five good nights; fires on the one bad night. The threshold sits 6.25x above the highest observed baseline and 3.3x below the incident - the widest margin available. 0.30 is not curve-fitted: it is independently defensible as 'nearly a third of the suite could not be measured', and ANY value in (0.05, 1.0] separates this corpus, so the choice is robust to the exact number. Gate runs BEFORE per-benchmark classification; on INVALID no verdict lines are emitted at all; exit code stays 0 (an invalid run is a loud classification, not a crash - same posture as the flake-guard sprint's DEGRADED history).
metadata.decision_departures: DELIBERATE DEPARTURE FROM ISSUE #524, flagged for the controller: #524 proposes 'infra fraction exceeds a threshold OR the pass total falls outside the trailing window'. I implement the FIRST DISJUNCT ONLY and REJECT the second. A pass-rate-collapse trigger cannot distinguish 'we failed to measure the subject' from 'the subject genuinely broke catastrophically'. A real compiler regression breaking 40 of 42 benchmarks has the SAME pass-rate signature as this outage - under the OR rule the detector would declare the run INVALID and file nothing on the single most important night in the project's history. That is a silent fallback on data that drives decisions, which CLAUDE.md section 2 forbids outright. The infra-taint fraction is a DIRECT measurement of unmeasurability (the harness told us it could not reach the model), so it is safe to gate on. Pass-rate deviation is retained as a REPORTED corroborating statistic in the INVALID notification ('pass rate 0.167 vs trailing median 0.643') but never triggers the gate. If the controller wants the OR rule anyway, say so before M2 - but then the failure mode above must be written into #524 as an accepted risk.
metadata.decision_mixed_trials: A benchmark is infra-tainted if ANY trial's category is in INFRA_CATEGORIES; tainted benchmarks are never filed. THE CONSEQUENCE, WEIGHED: a benchmark whose only clean signal is one trial has n=1. ACCEPTED - it is already the house position. classify_bench's min_trials=4 exists precisely because the sibling sprint concluded a single trial cannot certify anything (its headline defect was 'was_solid_in_prev certifies solid from ONE trial'). Filing a GitHub issue off one surviving trial while the other trial proves the infrastructure was broken is the same error in a new place. MEASURED COST: ~0.8 suppressed persistent-failures per normal night, 4 across five nights (13%). NAMED COST: the flake-guard's showcase csv_to_json escalation is DELAYED one night (F-3), not lost.
metadata.decision_history_remediation: CHOSEN: adopt the M-EVAL-MEASUREMENT-CONTRACT vocabulary VERBATIM, flag the 42 rows IN PLACE, filter at read time. Do not delete, do not rewrite the numbers. REJECTED (a) leave it and accept ~5 polluted nights - R-B measured 12/42 wrong verdicts, 10 silent false negatives, on a detector whose entire purpose is the solid->broken case; REJECTED (b) delete the 42 rows - violates the contract's D4 (never delete data; the invalid row is evidence of the bug). CONTRACT TRANSCRIBED: field "validity":{"valid":false,"reason":"infra_outage"} written ONLY on invalid rows; ABSENT MEANS VALID (load-bearing - 210 of the 252 live records predate this sprint; treating absent as invalid erases the entire history from every window, exactly as validity.go:65-75 warns); reuse zero_files as-is; add exactly ONE new constant infra_outage, also added to internal/eval_harness/validity.go so there remains ONE vocabulary, not two; loader split mirrors the Go API (load_history filters by default, load_history_including_invalid opts back in). BACKFILL: --mark-invalid DATE --reason R [--note TEXT], through the existing HistoryLock + atomic_write_history (no new concurrency surface). The SPRINT DOES NOT run it against live state - M3 tests it on a copy; the live run is a deployment step with a pre-flight cp backup.
metadata.top_risk: R-1 THE DATA-LOSS TRAP: update_history (:398-424) rebuilds the whole file from load_history(path) then atomic_write_history. If load_history starts filtering invalid rows, the very NEXT nightly at 05:00 silently DELETES all 42 invalid rows - turning a data-quality fix into permanent data loss and violating D4. update_history, history_health and bootstrap_history must all call load_history_including_invalid. This is a one-word change in a function nobody re-reads, and EVERY TEST PASSES without it - the deletion only manifests on the next real run. Guarded by the dedicated named test M3.4 plus mutation-proof M3.7(a), and re-checked in production at runbook step 5.

metadata.mutation_hygiene: For every 'must fail on today's code' criterion: state which mutation form was run; assert the edit matched EXACTLY ONCE (grep -c before/after); print the diff into the commit message or this file's notes; confirm the mutated file still IMPORTS (python3 -c 'import nightly_classify') so a syntax error cannot be mistaken for a caught mutant; revert and re-run green.
metadata.migration: 1. Merge to dev; rig pulls. 2. BACK UP FIRST: cp ~/.ailang/state/nightly-eval-history.jsonl{,.bak-20260729}. 3. Run the backfill ONCE, manually, BEFORE the next 05:00 nightly: python3 tools/nightly_classify.py --mark-invalid 2026-07-29 --reason infra_outage --note '...'. 4. Verify: wc -l still 252; grep -c infra_outage == 42; classifier read-only reports '1 invalid night excluded' on the HEALTH line. 5. First nightly after: confirm the file STILL has all 42 invalid rows (M3.4's real-world echo) and verdicts match the 07-29-removed baseline.
